about.title: Tehama Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Tehama is a small town, and a sudden loss here is felt by nearly everyone. Public records for 2025 show 4 injury collisions and no traffic deaths in the city itself, but families in this part of Tehama County still lose loved ones on the roads that run through and around it. Collision counts are highest along State Route 36, State Route 32, and South Avenue, and reported crashes cluster on Fridays between midnight and 2 a.m. A wrongful death claim in California is a civil action, entirely separate from any criminal case, and it belongs to specific people: the spouse or domestic partner and children come first, followed by certain dependents and heirs. Recoverable losses can include funeral and burial costs, the financial support the person would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. Two years from the date of death is the general deadline, and it is shorter when a government entity is involved. LawProactive is not a law firm. We simply connect you with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency.

items.question: My relative died in a crash on State Route 36 near Tehama. Does a wrongful death case depend on criminal charges?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and moves forward independently of any criminal case the district attorney may or may not pursue. Even if no charges are filed, your family may still have a civil claim based on negligence. An attorney can review the collision report and explain how the two processes differ.

items.question: What can a family actually recover in a California wrongful death case?
items.answer: Recoverable losses include funeral and burial costs and the financial support the person would reasonably have provided over their lifetime. California also recognizes the loss of love, companionship, comfort, and guidance. The specific value depends on the facts of your family's situation, and no outcome can be promised.

items.question: How long do we have to act in Tehama County?
items.answer: In most cases the deadline is two years from the date of death, not the date of the incident. If a city, county, or state agency may be at fault, a claim usually has to be presented much sooner, often within six months. Because of that shorter window, it helps to speak with an attorney early even if you are not ready to make decisions.
